Engineers’ role in autonomous workflows; UALink over UCIe; GDDR7; on-device speech filtering.

October 14th, 2026 -

By: Jesse Allen

Synopsys’ Thomas Andersen finds that as more execution moves into autonomous workflows, the engineer’s focus is shifting toward defining objectives, guiding decisions, evaluating tradeoffs, and determining whether an outcome is ready to move forward.
Siemens’ Sriram Bhaskar Teja Mundru shows how UALink over UCIe 3.0 improves cross-vendor interoperability and enables the development of scalable AI systems by standardizing interfaces, form factors, and flow control mechanisms.
Cadence’s Shyam Sharma discusses key features of the GDDR7 standard, including channel operation, encoding and signaling, the command and clock model, and protection mechanisms.
Arm’s Ben Clark combines LiteRT, quantization, KleidiAI, and SME2 to improve on-device toxic speech detection on mobile, reducing latency and server processing demand overall.
Keysight’s Mike Wager considers how to validate that an application works correctly across the full range of devices, operating systems, browsers, and environments people use to reach it, without supporting an individual test suite for each platform.
SEMI’s Marta Scandella reports from a recent event that explored how collaboration between academic institutions and employers can open the semiconductor sector to a broader, more inclusive talent pool.
Plus, check out the blogs featured in the latest Test, Measurement & Analytics newsletter:
Onto Innovation’s Yong Gao explores how complementary inspection and metrology help detect and identify smaller defects.
Nordson’s Kobe Zhang shows how optimized plasma processingv improves surface roughening and activation.
Teradyne’s Ben Mitchel explains why it’s essential to test every AI and data center device under real-world conditions.
Advantest’s Don Ong sits down with ISIG’s Salah Nasri to discuss why the next generation of industry leaders may be very different from the last.
